subject: Runtime artifact handling and custody questions (PegasusPay)
messages:
From: Amir Rahman <amir@pegasuspay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate and latency spike - request for logs and evidence

Jordan —

We observed a sustained latency increase and a spike in 5xx errors on our checkout flows between 08:40–09:05 PDT. Our SREs captured sample request traces and we need audit-grade artifacts now for our compliance team and upstream regulators. Specifically, can you provide:

- Server-side runtime logs (token-level/trace-backed) for the window 08:30–09:20 PDT, with timestamps preserved.
- Any KV-cache invalidation events or model fallbacks that happened in that window.
- A list of Redwood staff who accessed or exported logs during the incident (who touched the artifacts).
- SHA256 hashes for any archives you provide and a signed statement about retention policy for these artifacts.

We’re elevating this to our security/compliance team — they need the package and chain-of-custody details within 6 hours. Attachments: we’ve included sample request IDs (txn-sample-reqs.csv).

Thanks,
Amir Rahman
Head of Production Engineering
PegasusPay

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amir Rahman <amir@pegasuspay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and latency spike - request for logs and evidence

Hi Amir —

Thank you for the heads up and for the sample request IDs. We’re treating this as a high-priority escalation. Immediate plan:

1) Marcus / Eng will prepare a timestamped log artifact for 08:30–09:20 PDT and include kernel-level runtime traces + model routing events.
2) Security (Karthik) will produce an audit statement and the initial chain-of-custody manifest, and will take custody of the artifacts once they’re packaged.
3) I’ll deliver the package link and SHA256 checksums to you and confirm retention window and access controls.

Can you confirm whether PegasusPay requires a notarized or lawyer-signed affidavit, or will the standard signed chain-of-custody we provide suffice? Also confirm the delivery method you prefer (SFTP with signed keys, Drive link + access log, or direct Upload to Pegasus S3).

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Karthik —

PegasusPay has requested audit-grade artifacts for an 08:30–09:20 PDT window; they need the package and chain-of-custody within 6 hours. Items requested by customer: logs, KV/cache events, model-fallback records, list of Redwood staff who accessed artifacts, SHA256 hashes, and a retention statement.

Please prioritize:
- Marcus: produce a read-only artifact bundle (runtime-logs-2026-09-02.tar.gz stub) containing: per-request traces linked to request IDs (they provided a csv), model routing events, and any autoscaler messages. Include metadata files with exact collection commands and the system time sync snapshot (NTP).
- Karthik: generate a custody manifest template and indicate who will be the official custodian (security team member). Include a signed PGP fingerprint for the person who will upload the artifact.

Constraints / notes:
- Do NOT include full customer PII unnecessarily. If any logs contain transaction payloads, redact per our standard redaction matrix (see internal runbook link below). Provide the redaction checklist applied.
- Preserve original timestamps and system offsets in the bundle (don’t normalize to UTC in the logs themselves; include a conversion table).
- We may need to produce a formal retention hold for these artifacts if legal requests arrive. Naomi, please advise on timeline for placing a legal hold.

Internal runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/incident-artifact-handling (restricted)

Jordan

Subject: Incident artifact delivery plan + custody confirmation (PegasusPay)

Amir —

Thanks for your patience. Quick status and delivery plan:

- Package prepared: runtime-logs-2026-09-02.tar.gz (package contains per-request traces, routing events, collection metadata, and the redaction checklist).
- Custodian: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.com). Marcus will PGP-sign the manifest and provide SHA256 checksums for each file.
- Retention statement: Redwood will retain the incident artifact for 90 days by default for escalations of this type; if PegasusPay needs a longer retention window for audit, we can extend to 1 year under a signed data processing addendum.
- Delivery method: we can SFTP to your endpoint, or provide a Drive link with audit logs. Please confirm SFTP details if you prefer that route. After delivery, we will capture access logs and include them in the manifest.

A couple of compliance points we want to be explicit about:
1) Access history: any Redwood employee who requests the artifact will be logged; currently only Marcus has exported the package. If Legal requests an expanded custodian list, we’ll record it and update the manifest.
2) Redaction scope: we removed direct cardholder data and replaced it with tokenized IDs; the redaction checklist is included in the package.
3) Chain-of-custody: Marcus will create a signed, timestamped custody-transfer PDF when we hand the package to PegasusPay (or upload to your SFTP).

Please reply with preferred delivery method and whether PegasusPay needs a notarized affidavit or lawyer signature on the custody PDF. We’ll act immediately on your instruction.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
